name: iv_rank_low_sticky_put_credit_spread_v1
hypothesis: When implied volatility is very low relative to its recent history, the market persistently overprices short-dated put options because institutional demand for downside protection is sticky and slow to unwind even in calm regimes. This leaves the variance risk premium elevated and put credit spreads rich relative to the subdued realized path, a structural feature of the options market that is not arbitraged away quickly. Selling a defined-risk put credit spread in such low-IV states harvests this premium with rapid theta decay and limited tail risk.
selection_rule: the only ACCEPT among 40 hypotheses in campaign run-b8818e2a-1; 172 option hypotheses across 3 campaigns all time
exit_convention: Held to expiry. There is no stop, no profit target, no roll and no management rule, because the research data cannot price one: a specific contract is re-quoted on 1-3% of later sessions. Settlement is modelled European-style against the underlying's close on the expiration date; SPY options are American, so early assignment is real, is not modelled, and belongs to the executor.

sealed.note: 32 independent cycles settled inside the window; specs/10 D8 -- this window can refute and cannot confirm

can_refute_not_confirm: about 25 independent 28-DTE cycles: entitled to say this stopped working, never entitled to say it works (specs/10 D8)
